clue.text: Crow Indian-woman to the rear of Mohawk

parts.note: squaw is a dated (now offensive) word for a Native American woman

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter, taken here from Mohawk

explanation.surface: A Native American woman stands behind a Mohawk warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crow' looks like a tribe alongside Mohawk, but it is a verb, the definition. The final letter of Mohawk, K, follows SQUAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow and to squawk are both to make a loud harsh cry.

clue.text: Bishop, in appeal for help, has right pitiful tale

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for bishop inside the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation
Tories are the right-wing party in British politics

explanation.surface: A bishop's plea for aid includes a heartrending story.
explanation.walkthrough: TORY is the British Conservative, the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a sad account told to win sympathy.

clue.text: Beaten man rued being defenceless

indicators.note: beaten, like eggs whisked up, means the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A defeated man regretted being without protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' rearranges MAN RUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means carrying no weapons, so unable to protect oneself.

clue.text: Possibly Californian playing partners get less tolerant

parts.note: in bridge West and East (W and E) play as partners
sterner means stricter, more severe

explanation.surface: Card partners from California grow harsher with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge seats are named by compass points, with W and E one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from California lives in the American West, so is one example of a western American.

clue.text: Take a chance in a manner of speaking, turning to son

parts.note: a drawl is a slow, lengthened way of talking

indicators.note: turning means the little word to is read backwards in place

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

explanation.surface: Someone gambles on their way of talking as they turn to address their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes OT from 'to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing lots settles a matter by chance, so it means risking the outcome on luck.

clue.text: Campanologists like to introduce a little variety

definitions.meaning: what bell-ringers enjoy doing: ringing every permutation on the bells
to vary things, try something new

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers enjoy mixing things up a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Campanologists are bell-ringers; changes are the ordered sequences rung on a peal of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Bell-ringers work through sequences called changes, and the phrase is also an idiom for varying one's routine.

clue.text: Steward has forgotten one drink

indicators.note: has forgotten means the word for steward drops the following piece

parts.note: a steward serves at table, like a waiter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The steward has forgotten someone's drink order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Water is the commonest thing people drink.

clue.text: Plant obscuring good view

indicators.note: obscuring means the plant hides the word for good inside itself

parts.note: the onion is a bulb plant
pi, short for pious, means good in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A plant blocking a fine view.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a standard abbreviation for good.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is one's view on something.

clue.text: Pin that's more distorted

definitions.meaning: a pointed rod for holding things together, as in cooking
more crooked or slanting, the comparative of an adjective meaning askew

explanation.surface: A pin that is more bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'skew' as an adjective and adds -er.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a long pin for holding meat, and something skewer is more askew.

clue.text: Club relearnt by righting bloomer

indicators.note: righting means putting the jumbled letters to rights in a new order

explanation.surface: A club relearns its ways by correcting a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canterbury bell is a garden flower, a campanula, so a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Tugs told to slacken off by ship's officer

parts.note: tugs are small boats

indicators.note: told signals that what follows is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: to wane is to diminish or slacken off

explanation.surface: Tugboats are instructed to ease off by an officer on board.
explanation.walkthrough: WANE said aloud gives WAIN, an old word for a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A bosun, the petty officer in charge of a ship's rigging and deck crew.

clue.text: Wind and wet in…

annotationWithheld.why: Wind and wet in... (5): TWINE is an anagram of WET IN, but the anagram indicator is 'storm' in the continuation clue 12-across, so no word in this clue can signal it without 'Wind' doing two jobs

clue.text: … storm produced on stage

definitions.meaning: a storm is a violent wind and rain
a play performed in a theatre, here Shakespeare's last solo work

explanation.surface: A storm is staged in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues 11-across, whose ellipsis runs into this clue. 'The Tempest' is Shakespeare's play, so the second definition is something put on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent gale is a tempest; Shakespeare's play of that name is regularly performed in theatres.

clue.text: Insect-its tail could be I metre

annotationWithheld.why: Insect-its tail could be I metre (7): the answer's own tail ERMITE is an anagram of I METRE, but the leading T comes from no clue word (it is the answer's head), so the grammar has no honest form for it
annotationWithheld.clue: Insect-its tail could be I metre

clue.text: Salient feature of endangered animal

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The most striking characteristic of a threatened species.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salient feature' reads as one phrase meaning a notable trait; split it, and 'Salient' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In fortification a redan is a V-shaped work projecting outward, which is what a salient is.

clue.text: Last bit of weed devoured by swimming bird

indicators.note: devoured by means the next piece is swallowed inside the word for swimming

parts.note: a head that is swimming is reeling

indicators.note: the last bit of weed is its final letter

explanation.surface: A bird swimming along gulps down the end of a strand of pondweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' looks like it describes the bird, but it means REELING, as in a swimming head.
explanation.definitionFit: The reedling, or bearded tit, is a small reed-bed songbird.

clue.text: Osculates promiscuously — a hopeless endeavour

indicators.note: promiscuously means indiscriminately, so the letters are mixed up at random

explanation.surface: Kissing all and sundry is a futile pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Osculates' means kisses; 'promiscuously' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is an effort with no hope of success.

clue.text: State bank holds silver in a small way

indicators.note: holds means the state and the bank together contain the next piece

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, a US state
to bank on is to rely on
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A state bank keeps only a little silver in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' is a verb, as in 'bank on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagrely means scantily or sparingly, doing things in a small way.

clue.text: Complete, as a result of being without nothing

indicators.note: being without here means lying outside, so the phrase for as a result of wraps round the next piece

parts.note: through can mean because of, as in 'through no fault of his own'
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Something is whole only because it lacks nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside', not 'lacking'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough work is complete in every detail.

clue.text: Cutter hired to gnome

parts.note: hack as an adjective means hired, as in a hack writer
a gnome is a pithy saying, as is a saw

explanation.surface: A cutter rented for a garden gnome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gnome' is not a garden ornament but an old word for a maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed saw for metal, a tool that cuts.

clue.text: Island's turned dark

indicators.note: turned means the letters of the island's name with its 's are read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the island of Napoleon's exile; 's adds S

explanation.surface: An island has become gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba, the Mediterranean island, plus 's gives ELBAS, which 'turned' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is a poetic and heraldic word for black.

clue.text: Security provided primarily for an official

parts.note: bail is money given as security for a defendant's return
provided means on condition that, if

indicators.note: primarily means first, so take the opening letter of for

explanation.surface: Security arrangements made mainly for an officeholder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the F of 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailiff is a court officer who serves writs and seizes goods.

clue.text: A fellow gets Sally frightened

parts.note: a sally is a sudden attack, a raid

explanation.surface: A man gets a girl called Sally scared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a woman's name; as a common noun it is a sortie from a besieged place.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid means scared or fearful.

clue.text: Hearing, perhaps, the members of a profession'

definitions.meaning: hearing is one example of a bodily sense or power
a group of professionals, such as a university's teachers or a country's lawyers

explanation.surface: A court hearing is attended by members of a profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing, perhaps' suggests a court case; it is one of the five senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty is a natural power such as sight or hearing, and also the body of members of a profession, like a university's teaching staff.

clue.text: Doctor demanding a pound per person, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a pound is L, and per person is each, so L EACH

explanation.surface: A doctor who charges a pound a head.
explanation.walkthrough: L EACH (a pound each) sounds like leech; a greedy doctor is a leech in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech is an old word for a physician, from the bloodsucking worms they applied.

clue.text: Taking not entirely satisfactory honour

indicators.note: not entirely says the word for satisfactory loses its final letter

parts.note: nice can mean pleasant or satisfactory
in card games the king is one of the honours, the top cards

explanation.surface: Accepting an award that is not quite good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and whist the honours are the ace, king, queen, jack and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicking is slang for stealing, which is taking without permission.

clue.text: One's overcome by drink in the passage

indicators.note: overcome by means the first piece is swamped, sitting inside the word for drink

parts.note: ale is beer
one is I, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: Someone is overcome by drink while out in the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I plus 's.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage.

clue.text: Expensive flower — attractive girl receives five

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the Exe flows through Devon

indicators.note: receives means the word for attractive girl takes the next piece into it

parts.note: cutie is slang for a pretty girl
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: An expensive bloom, as a pretty girl is given five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a river, a crossword stand-by. 'Expensive' fits in the sense of an executive car or flat, made for the well-paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Executive as an adjective means upmarket and costly, as in executive homes.

clue.text: Olympic event in decline

definitions.meaning: an Alpine skiing race straight down a mountain course

explanation.surface: An Olympic race is losing popularity.
explanation.walkthrough: The downhill is the Alpine ski race; a thing going downhill is getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: The downhill is a fast Alpine ski race at the Winter Games, and a business going downhill is deteriorating.

clue.text: Be left with fish — 5 here

parts.note: taken as written
fry are young fish

explanation.surface: Someone is left holding a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 here' points to 5-down: bell-ringers change-ringing do it in this tower room.
explanation.definitionFit: A belfry is the bell chamber of a tower, where change-ringers perform.
